audit_notes: Model: steady advection-diffusion of absorbing dirt in a frame attached to the receding (eroding) surface; material moves towards the surface at the erosion rate v and dirt spreads into the top layer with effective diffusivity D = dirt_penetration_depth * v, so the dirt profile decays as exp(-z/delta). Surface: deposition flux minus rain/wind wash-off (first-order, wash_off_velocity * c(0)); deep boundary clean. Closed form: c(0) = J_dep/(v + k_w), areal load m = c(0)*delta. Metric: integral of c over the layer times domain_depth = areal dirt load (kg/m2); transform to the daily-mean interior heat flux through the roof with alpha = 1 - SR_clean + k_abs*m (same sol-air/U model as the other roof concepts). Checks: Peclet number of the layer v*L/D = L/delta = 10 (profile fully resolved, c(1)=0 valid). Erosion 20 um/yr (6.3e-13 m/s) is at the high end of chalking mineral paints; historic chalking TiO2 paints lost 5-20 um/yr; in arid climates erosion needs UV plus wind/sand rather than rain, so this value is uncertain by a factor ~3. Baseline acrylic erosion 0.5 um/yr (1.6e-14 m/s) is typical of durable acrylics. k_abs is calibrated so the baseline reproduces the CRRC-type aged loss 0.85 -> 0.67, so the baseline is anchored to data, but the design benefit then follows almost directly from the ratio (v_b + k_w)/(v_d + k_w) = 0.22 - it is an input-ratio model, not independent physics, and should be judged as such. Hand check: design m = 2e-11*5e-6/7.9e-13 = 1.27e-4 kg/m2 -> dAlpha 0.040 -> SR 0.88 -> q = 0.5*(36 + 150 - 78.2)/15.5 = 3.48 W/m2; baseline m = 5.68e-4 -> dAlpha 0.18 -> q = 5.56 W/m2; gain ~37 %. Service life: 0.8 mm at 20 um/yr lasts 40 years, OK. Structural: a deliberately weak (chalking) matrix has low cohesion and abrasion resistance; hail and foot traffic damage roofs; runoff of BaSO4/CaCO3 fines is non-toxic but whitens gutters/facades below. Simulation coefficient: effective dirt removal velocity v + k_w = 7.9e-13 m/s.
